text:
maria: quick question — noticed weird auth merge when creating two Python clients in the same process. one client is supposed to use API_KEY_A, the other API_KEY_B, but requests sometimes go out with A for both.

alex: oof. can you share minimal repro? async or sync?

maria: async. gist in a sec. basically:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
# env: REDWOOD_API_KEY=A
client_a = RedwoodClient(api_key='A')
client_b = RedwoodClient(api_key='B')
await client_a.generate(... )  # sometimes sends B
```

olga: are you using any global session or a helper that wraps clients? we've seen pockets where aiohttp connector is shared and a custom auth hook mutates headers.

maria: no wrapper, plain import. only thing is we rotate env in tests (setenv) and create clients after changing env.

tim: can repro locally. looks like credential providers are being cached on import path. creating a second client with explicit api_key should override, but our async cache uses the env-backed provider keying by process and reuses it across instances.

alex: that's a bug then — clients must prefer explicit constructor args over cached providers. priority: explicit > provided credential provider instance > env provider > profile.

maria: agreed. also typing-wise it's unclear: constructor accepts Union[str, CredentialProvider], but the docs only show string. could we add an explicit Credentials class in the SDK to make intent clearer?

olga: feature req: accept credentials_factory: Callable[[], CredentialProvider] so tests can inject ephemeral creds cleanly. avoids global singletons.

tim: patch idea: change provider cache key to include the client id or a unique client instance token when api_key is passed explicitly, and short-circuit cache lookup if api_key param is not None. cheap fix.

maria: repro log attached: headers show Authorization: Bearer B even when client_a created first.

devex-bot: Deploy bot detected: release 0.4.7 was deployed 2026-01-09.

alex: okay. i'll file an issue and add a unit test for multi-client auth mixing + an async integration test that toggles os.environ during runtime. tagging @eng-ml for visibility re: credential provider design.

tim: for immediate mitigation, add note in README: "Do not rely on env var rotation to create per-client credentials in a single process; pass api_key or a credentials provider instance to each client."

maria: thanks. one more ask — can we expose a debug flag to dump which credential provider each client resolved to (env vs explicit vs cache)? would make debugging easier.

alex: good idea. I'll add a client._debug_auth_source property behind a feature flag. will include typing for it as Optional[str] in stub files.

olga: adding to the SDK backlog: (1) fix cache behavior, (2) add credentials_factory, (3) docs + debug flag, (4) typing improvements.

maria: awesome, thanks folks :thumbsup:

tim: created issue #4123 — link: https://internal.redwood/issue/4123 — assigning to @alex.

alex: will send a PR with tests later today.

maria: will bake this into our onboarding sample app so new users don't hit it during evals.
